oneLine: Congressional elections proceeded on Nov 3 as voting took place amid the Binance hack aftermath; Bitcoin and Ethereum each gained about 0.8–0.9% intraday, and market breadth held strong at 70% of coins up despite election-day uncertainty.
caveman: On Nov 3, Americans voted for Congress (the results wouldn't be known until after midnight that night). During the day, Binance revealed how hackers had stolen $6.3 billion: they used fake job interviews to trick developers into downloading malicious code. Bitcoin went up 0.8% and Ethereum went up 0.9% by the end of the trading day, and most crypto coins were up (70% of them). But during the day there was a scary moment—early on, Bitcoin dropped and over $200 million in traders' risky bets got wiped out (liquidations). Then prices recovered. In Korea and Hong Kong, big tech companies' stock futures fell hard—SK Hynix dropped 7.6% and Samsung dropped 5.6%, probably because of election uncertainty and worries about US tech policy. Another exchange, Mercado Bitcoin in Brazil, also got hacked for $46 million that same day. It was a tense day, but the market held up.
priceVolumeSummary: Bitcoin and Ethereum both gained roughly 0.8–0.9% on the day across all major venues, which stayed closely aligned on prices. Binance led volume for both assets, moving $8.46 billion of BTC and $5.57 billion of ETH.
positioningSummary: Bitcoin traders held a bullish long-to-short bias of 2.57:1 across all accounts and 1.87:1 among the largest traders, with funding positive at 3.16% annualized on Binance. Bitcoin open interest rose 0.48% in USD terms despite a slight decline in coins held. Ethereum showed stronger long positioning at 2.64:1 on Binance but carried negative funding of -1.49% annually, signaling caution on further upside. Both assets saw modest taker buy pressure (1.02 and 1.05 ratios respectively), and 70.4% of Binance perpetual contracts closed up for the day, reflecting broad strength despite sharp intraday volatility tied to election uncertainty and hack liquidations. Market sentiment remained fearful (26 on the Fear & Greed Index, down from 37 the prior day).
stocksSummary: Korean semiconductor exporters fell sharply during Nov 3: SK Hynix dropped 7.6% and Samsung Electronics fell 5.6%, likely on election uncertainty and pre-election concerns about potential US technology policy shifts. Hong Kong index products tracking these names fell harder, with leveraged products down 14–15%. Chinese markets saw mixed movement with Unitree Robotics up 2.5% and CXMT up 5.9%.

movers.explanation: AGT surged 32.9% intraday despite losing 27.4% over the prior 24 hours, a sharp reversal suggesting possible exchange listing event or liquidation cascade.
HOT rallied 25.9% intraday after declining 19.1% in the broader 24-hour window, a similar reversal pattern to AGT with no clear public announcement.
BMT gained 23.6% on the day amid positive 24-hour performance. No clear catalyst identified.

topThree.headline: Binance reveals hack attack vector: fake job interviews used to compromise developer credentials
topThree.what: Binance disclosed operational details of the Oct 31–Nov 1 $6.34 billion breach on Nov 3. Attackers posed as recruiters, used fake job interviews to deliver malicious code through coding assignments, then exploited stolen deployment credentials to access wallet signing systems. The exchange had covered 98% of affected assets and launched withdrawal phase 2 at 04:00 GMT Nov 3. Net outflows declined from a $7B peak to $3.5B by day's end, and the deposit-to-withdrawal ratio recovered to 78%, signaling stabilization.

topThree.headline: Crypto markets show sharp intraday volatility on election day; over $200M in leveraged longs liquidated
topThree.what: During Nov 3 election day voting, cryptocurrency markets experienced sharp intraday moves tied to election-result uncertainty and the ongoing Binance hack discourse. Bitcoin retreated to below $77,000 in early Asia trading (down >1% in under 2 hours) with over $200 million in leveraged long positions liquidated, before recovering as voting progress eased concerns. By early evening Nov 3, BTC had recovered and the market closed higher for the day.

topThree.headline: Mercado Bitcoin breach adds second exchange hack to Nov 3 risk narrative; $46 million stolen
topThree.what: Brazilian cryptocurrency exchange Mercado Bitcoin fell victim to a $46 million attack on Nov 3 UTC, suspending deposits and withdrawals while the company stated it would cover all losses. The breach occurred the same day election voting was underway and as market participants were still absorbing the Binance hack details, heightening security concerns across the sector.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Binance hack attack vector revealed: fake job interviews and malicious code in coding assignments
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Binance disclosed on Nov 3 that the $6.34 billion breach used social engineering and targeted developers. Attackers impersonated recruiters, delivered malicious code through fake job interview coding tasks, and exploited stolen credentials to access wallet signing systems. By Nov 3 UTC, 98% of affected assets were covered and withdrawal phase 2 had launched, stabilizing the market.

Hacks, exploits and outages.headline: Mercado Bitcoin hit with $46 million theft; company pledges to cover all losses
Hacks, exploits and outages.what: Brazilian exchange Mercado Bitcoin suffered a $46 million hack on Nov 3 UTC, forcing suspension of deposits and withdrawals. The exchange stated it would compensate all affected users, though the incident coincided with heightened security scrutiny following the Binance breach.

Regulation and policy.headline: SEC clarifies crypto-asset governance FAQs; Hong Kong plans 24/7 tokenized settlement trials with stablecoins
Regulation and policy.what: The SEC released new clarifying guidance on identifying central parties in token governance structures. In parallel, Hong Kong's Monetary Authority advanced plans for 24/7 tokenized settlement infrastructure, signaling intent to include stablecoins in trials involving Exchange Fund Bills—a development potentially significant for on-chain finance.

glossary.definition: The price difference between the current market price (spot price) and the futures price for the same asset.
The percentage of assets in a market that are moving up or down in price; high breadth (e.g., 70% of coins up) suggests strong market-wide sentiment.
A sentiment indicator ranging from 0 (Extreme Fear) to 100 (Extreme Greed) that measures cryptocurrency market emotion based on volatility, momentum, and social media trends.

A periodic payment between long and short traders on perpetual futures, designed to keep the contract price close to the spot price. Positive funding means longs pay shorts; negative means shorts pay longs.
Forced closure of a leveraged position when collateral drops below the exchange's minimum requirement; common in derivatives markets where a price move against a trader wipes out their margin.
The ratio of traders holding long positions (betting price will rise) to those holding short positions (betting price will fall); ratios above 1.0 indicate more bullish positioning.
The reference price used to calculate funding and liquidations on futures exchanges, typically a weighted average of spot prices or index-based price.
The total value of all outstanding long and short positions in a futures market; growth in OI suggests increasing leverage and potential volatility.
The day-over-day percentage shift in total open interest, indicating whether traders are adding or reducing positions collectively.
Futures contracts with no expiry date, allowing traders to hold leveraged long or short positions indefinitely as long as they maintain collateral and pay funding rates.
The ratio of market buy orders to sell orders; ratios above 1.0 indicate more aggressive buying by takers (traders accepting current ask prices).
The long-to-short ratio among the largest traders on an exchange, indicating whether the biggest players are leaning bullish or bearish.
